Question B-003-016-010.

Why the correct answer is right: In series, matched battery voltages add while the ampere-hour capacity stays that of one string. Think of cells end to end in a flashlight: two 12 V, 20 Ah batteries in series make 24 V at 20 Ah.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "24 volts, 40 ampere-hours": The voltage is the series value, but the capacity has been incorrectly added as if the batteries were in parallel.
- sourceIndex 2: "12 volts, 40 ampere-hours": This is the parallel result, where voltage stays at 12 V and ampere-hours add.
- sourceIndex 3: "6 volts, 80 ampere-hours": Series connection does not halve voltage or multiply capacity by four. Both parts of this result use the wrong relationship.
